top_categories.workout_context: 6,800ft of climbing makes aerobic ceiling relevant when the grade or pace changes. VO2max work supports those hard moments; sustained climbing and conservative pacing remain the spine.
73ft/mi signals a climbing-heavy course. Sustained sub-threshold and threshold work builds the steady power needed without turning the opening climb into the day’s hardest effort.
Race-pace efforts that mimic Gran Fondo Utah's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before June.

Road-specific control matters at Gran Fondo Utah. Practice on mixed terrain: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 93 miles.
At Gran Fondo Utah, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Gran Fondo Utah. Train it until it feels boring.
At mile 60 of 93, glycogen is gone. This workout teaches your body to produce watts on fumes.
6,800ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.
Every hard session works better with a bigger aerobic base. At 93 miles, base fitness is the difference between racing and surviving.
Brief efforts above sustainable power can come from grade changes, positioning, or closing a gap at Gran Fondo Utah. Train them without letting those efforts derail the longer pacing plan.
Steeper ramps, positioning, or pace changes on mixed terrain can demand short hard efforts. Practice them without compromising the sustained work that defines the course.
Two threshold sessions per week without the recovery cost of VO2max work. For 93 miles, sustainable FTP gains matter more than peak power.

race_overlay.weather: June in Payson Memorial Park, 300 S Main St, Payson, UT 84651, USA — Early-mid June in Payson (Wasatch Front, ~4,500 ft): mild/warm daytime highs 70-85°F, possible afternoon thunderstorms at altitude. Rehearse adaptable layers and race-day kit changes in the final 2 weeks before Gran Fondo Utah. Use the organizer's current forecast and safety instructions for final choices.
race_overlay.nutrition: Target 60–80g carbs/hour for Gran Fondo Utah’s 93 miles. Start fueling within the first 30 minutes — early fueling prevents late-race collapse. Bonking at mile 60 is a nutrition failure, not a fitness failure.
race_overlay.altitude: Gran Fondo Utah includes meaningful altitude exposure. Reduced oxygen availability can affect sustainable power, pacing, and recovery. Use a conservative upper-mountain pacing plan, test any travel or acclimatization strategy before the event, and plan layers for changing conditions. Do not begin iron or other supplements without clinician-guided testing.
race_overlay.terrain: The course profile at Gran Fondo Utah rewards specific practice. Include regular rides on mixed terrain to build confidence.
